candidate_sources.README.md:
# Transit stop lookup

A shared per-key query cache provides subscribe(key,options) -> unique observer
handle, unsubscribe(handle), online(boolean), focus(boolean), snapshot(key),
and dispose() of observer scopes. Queries retain status (pending/success/error),
fetchStatus (idle/fetching/paused), and data. queryFn receives a lazy signal
accessor. Each actual access records consumption; each fetch owns its controller
and completion. Completion is asynchronous; initial online entry is synchronous,
paused continuation resumes on a Promise turn. First start uses network mode;
continuation also needs focus. 'always' can run offline; 'offlineFirst' allows
first offline entry but retry can pause. Retries use explicit scheduler handles.
Multiple observers share one fetch. Unconsumed active work can finish into cache
after its view departs; consumed work is physically abortable. Cancellation
reverts previous query data/status and settles the originating attempt. Late
fulfillment cannot become a new attempt's data. Unknown unsubscribe is inert.
The component owns observer scope; the cache remains outside individual views.
Dependency versions and build/test configuration are outside the repair scope.

Embedding API: bind registers a native callable; Environment.call
provides newAttempt(key,number), abort(key,number), request(key,number, lazy-read
token, completion token), defer(callback token), schedule(callback token,delay).
The request host calls queryFn with an actual AbortSignal property. Reading it
invokes the native consumption closure synchronously; Promise settlement later
invokes the native completion with {ok,value}. All observer, retry, cancellation,
state and cache logic executes in the target language. No native JS Promise or
DOM claim is made. Native object identity binds query and attempt generations;
wire handles only identify injected callbacks. 
Module cache and EventTarget subscription handles; actual Node16 promises

checkpoints: Before invoking queryFn from a paused continuation, verify that the originating attempt is still active and has an observer-authorized continuation.
When the last observer unsubscribes from a never-started paused attempt, make that attempt unable to resume on later online or focus events.
After reconnect, confirm that the offline-mounted-and-unmounted query remains uninvolved: queryFn is not called and no signal is exposed or consumed.
Verify that an unknown unsubscribe remains inert and that multiple current observers still share one fetch.
Verify that late completion from an older attempt cannot update a newer attempt's state.
forbidden_effects: Do not invoke the signal-consuming queryFn after reconnect for a fresh online-mode attempt whose only observer unsubscribed while the attempt was paused offline.
Do not allow a stale or settled attempt to publish data or status into a newer attempt.
Do not make refetchOnReconnect control the required cancellation behavior; the defect occurs independently of that option.
Do not abort unconsumed work that has already started solely because its last view departed; it may finish into the shared cache.
Do not change public interfaces, dependencies, runtime configuration, or build/test configuration.
Do not modify tests or configuration; product source is the only repair scope.
lifecycle_identity: A query is the per-key cache entry stored in Session.cache.
An attempt is the specific Attempt object assigned to q.attempt, with its own monotonically assigned number, controller, settlement state, previous state, options, and retry state.
Attempt validity requires object identity through q.attempt===a and an unsettled attempt; an attempt number or callback handle alone is not sufficient lifecycle identity.
Observer handles identify subscriptions and are distinct from query and attempt generations.
Unsubscribing the last observer is a lifecycle boundary for a never-started paused attempt; reconnect or focus changes must not revive that departed attempt.
A newly subscribed attempt for the same key is a new generation and must not accept an older attempt's completion.

obligations.text: A fresh online-mode query subscribed while offline may enter paused state without synchronously calling queryFn.

If that query's last observer unsubscribes before the paused initial attempt starts, the originating attempt must be settled or otherwise invalidated so later reconnect or focus processing cannot invoke queryFn for it.
The O2 behavior must hold independently of refetchOnReconnect.
Every completion or scheduled continuation must remain bound to the same active attempt generation; late fulfillment from an older attempt must not become a newer attempt's data.

Existing supported behavior must remain: paused continuation resumes on a Promise turn, first start follows network mode, continuation also requires focus, always may run offline, and offlineFirst may start offline but pause a retry.
Multiple observers of a key continue to share one fetch; removing one observer must not cancel work still observed by others.

Unconsumed work that has actually started may finish into the cache after its view departs, while consumed work remains physically abortable and cancellation reverts previous query state and settles its originating attempt.
Unknown unsubscribe remains inert, and dispose continues to dispose observer scopes without converting the shared cache into view-owned state.
Preserve the subscribe, unsubscribe, online, focus, snapshot, and dispose interfaces, as well as dependencies and build/test configuration; change product source only.

ordering_barriers: For the reported sequence—offline subscription, unsubscription of the last observer, then reconnect—the unsubscription boundary must invalidate the paused initial continuation before reconnect scans cached queries.
The paused-to-fetching transition must occur only after a Promise turn and only after rechecking the same attempt's validity and continuation authorization.
Attempt invalidation or settlement must precede any later queryFn invocation, retry scheduling, state publication, or signal exposure for that attempt.
Completion must verify active attempt identity before writing data, status, or fetchStatus.
A new attempt for the same cache key must replace the old attempt generation before its own results can be accepted.
preservation: Retain per-key shared caching and unique observer handles.
Retain status values pending/success/error, fetchStatus values idle/fetching/paused, and cached data behavior.
Retain synchronous initial online entry and asynchronous Promise-turn resumption for paused continuation.
Retain network-mode and focus eligibility rules described by the public README.
Retain lazy signal access: consumption is recorded only when queryFn reads the signal property.
Retain the distinction between unconsumed active work that may finish into cache and consumed work that can be physically aborted.
Retain cancellation rollback to the attempt's previous query data/status.
Retain retry scheduling behavior through explicit scheduler handles.
Retain inert handling of unknown unsubscribe and observer-scope disposal.
Retain Node 16.20.2, dependency-free configuration, and all public APIs.

This occurs independently of refetchOnReconnect.

First start uses network mode; continuation also needs focus. 'always' can run offline; 'offlineFirst' allows first offline entry but retry can pause.
Multiple observers share one fetch. Unconsumed active work can finish into cache after its view departs; consumed work is physically abortable.

active(q,a){return q.attempt===a&&!a.settled;}

resume(q){const a=q.attempt;if(a&&this.active(q,a)&&q.state.fetchStatus==='paused'&&this.eligible(a)&&!a.queued){a.queued=true;Promise.resolve().then(()=>{a.queued=false;if(!this.active(q,a))return;if(a.failures&&a.retryCancelled){a.settled=true;q.state={...q.state,status:'error',fetchStatus:'idle'};this.project(q);return;}this.invoke(q,a);});}}
if(q.observers.size===0){const a=q.attempt;if(a&&!a.settled){if(q.consumed)this.cancel(q,a);else a.retryCancelled=true;}}
online(value){this.connected=value;for(const q of this.cache.values())this.resume(q);}
cancel(q,a){if(a.settled)return;a.settled=true;q.state={...a.previous,fetchStatus:'idle'};a.controller.abort();this.project(q);}
These checks are required after an Action but do not test business behavior. Preserve original TASK and public README/source obligations.
